contract.words: Collect $4,000 of settled cash within 45 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $4,000 of settled cash in the owner's account within 45 days

strategy.title: No plan: the grant-application package has no price any buyer pays
strategy.why: The only opening's price fact is the state program's grant award (up to $5,000 per approved department, program notice 2026-10). That is money the program pays the department, not a price a department pays for an application package; no agreement, quote or payment for the package is recorded. Without a price, the number of deals needed and whether $4,000 can settle in 45 days cannot be computed, so no plan is established.

alternatives.title: Plan at $5,000 per package from the grant award figure
alternatives.why: Rejected: a grant is not a purchase price, and a department is unlikely to be able to pay its whole award for the application.

alternatives.title: Test-sell at an invented fee
alternatives.why: No price on record to anchor a fee; the gap is named and resolved first by measuring what departments pay.

card.payer: Volunteer fire chiefs and department treasurers
card.reachableChannel: Published department emails in the state fire marshal's registry
card.offerScope: A completed equipment-grant application package with the needs narrative and budget; delivered in 5 days.

facts.value: The state fire marshal's registry lists 540 volunteer fire departments, each eligible to apply in the current grant round.
Sell A completed equipment-grant application package with the needs narrative and budget; delivered in 5 days. to each buyer.
Volunteer fire chiefs and department treasurers
The state Volunteer Fire Assistance program awards each approved department a grant of up to $5,000 for equipment purchases (program notice, 2026-10).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is right and names the decisive gap correctly. The card's only price fact ($5,000) is the state Volunteer Fire Assistance program's grant award to an approved department - money the program pays the buyer, not a price the buyer pays for an application package. No agreement, quote or payment for the package is recorded, and the conversion fact (14 agreements of 200) states no price. Without a price the deals needed cannot be computed, so no link chain to $4,000 in 45 days exists. The plan does not mislabel this as a constraint (the evidence is missing, not proven insufficient), sets decisiveLinks = OFFER_AND_PRICE, and its resolution (find what departments pay and whether the program permits preparation fees, then offer to 100 registry departments and record paid orders) is the evidence that decides it. Every other link (540 registry departments, published emails, Brain-produced package, $20 cost, 10 days to cash in a 45-day window) is evidenced, so a price would make the opening plannable quickly.
findings: Price fact is a grant award (reward paid to the department), correctly rejected as a purchase price; planning at $5,000 would also be implausible since many grant programs bar paying preparation fees from the award.
decisiveLinks = [OFFER_AND_PRICE] matches Brain's only missing link; no unknown is treated as known; ledger is empty and no money is committed.

Suggestion for the next revision: once a fee is found, a CONDITIONAL test is startable - e.g. at fee F, deals needed = ceil(4000/F); at the 7% rate that needs ceil(4000/F)/0.07 contacts, which must be <= 540; also confirm whether the program allows a department to pay for preparation (an eligibility question that could itself be decisive).
Executor SEND_A_MESSAGE is NOT_CONNECTED for the test step.
